name: office-workbench
description: View Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files inside VS Code, and edit Word, Excel, PowerPoint and CSV files.

languageModelTools.name: officeWorkbench_readFile
languageModelTools.userDescription: Read a Word, Excel, PowerPoint or CSV file as Markdown.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads a Word (.docx/.docm), Excel (.xlsx/.xlsm), PowerPoint (.pptx/.pptm), CSV or TSV file and returns its content as text. Word: Markdown with headings, lists and tables. Excel: one Markdown table per sheet with displayed values (first column = row number, header = column letters; only rows with values are listed), followed by the sheet's formulas (cells filled down with the same formula are grouped, e.g. "E4:E7: =C4*D4") and merged ranges. PowerPoint: text, bullet lists and tables per slide, plus speaker notes. CSV/TSV: the raw text. If the file is open in the editor, unsaved changes are included. For large workbooks, pass `sheet` and/or `range` to read part of it. Before editing a Word document or PowerPoint presentation, read it with `outline: true` to get the paragraph numbers (Word) or slide numbers and shape ids (PowerPoint) that the editing tools use.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the file, or a path relative to the workspace folder.

sheet.description: Excel only: name of the sheet to read (default: all sheets).

range.description: Excel only: A1 range to read, e.g. "A1:F50" (default: whole sheet).

outline.description: Word/PowerPoint only: return the numbered outline used by the editing tools (Word: every paragraph, including table cells, numbered in reading order; PowerPoint: each slide's editable shapes with their ids and table cells) instead of Markdown.

maxCharacters.description: Maximum length of the returned text (default 40000).

languageModelTools.name: officeWorkbench_editSpreadsheet
languageModelTools.userDescription: Edit cells, rows, columns and sheets of an Excel workbook or CSV file.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Edits an Excel workbook (.xlsx/.xlsm) or a CSV/TSV file. The file is opened in the Office Workbench spreadsheet editor and each edit becomes an undoable step; changes stay unsaved for the user to review unless `save` is true. Other parts of the workbook (charts, images, macros, styles) are preserved. Edits are applied in order; if one fails, the earlier ones remain applied. Edit types: "setCells" with `cells` mapping A1 addresses to input text exactly as a user would type it (numbers like "1234.5", dates like "2026/1/15", percentages like "12.5%", TRUE/FALSE, formulas starting with "=", a leading apostrophe for literal text, "" to clear) — formulas are not calculated by the editor, Excel calculates them when the file is opened; in CSV files every value is stored as plain text. "clearRange" with `range` (e.g. "B2:D10"). "insertRows"/"deleteRows" with 1-based `row` and optional `count` (inserted rows go above `row`). "insertColumns"/"deleteColumns" with column letter `column` and optional `count`. Formulas, merged cells and chart ranges are adjusted for inserted/deleted rows and columns. Workbooks only: "addSheet" with optional `name`, "renameSheet" with `sheet` and new `name`, "deleteSheet" with `sheet`. `sheet` is the sheet name; when omitted, the first visible sheet is used. Read the file first with the read tool to find the right cells.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the workbook or CSV file, or a path relative to the workspace folder.

cells.description: setCells: map of A1 address to input text, e.g. {"B3": "42", "C3": "=B3*2"}.

save.description: Save the file after editing (default false: leave the changes unsaved for review).

languageModelTools.name: officeWorkbench_editDocument
languageModelTools.userDescription: Edit, insert, delete or replace text in paragraphs of a Word document.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Edits the text of a Word document (.docx/.docm). Read the file first with the read tool and `outline: true`: it numbers every paragraph (body and table cells, in reading order) and marks paragraphs that cannot be edited (with fields, hyperlinks, pictures, tracked changes, comments, content controls). The file is opened in the Office Workbench editor and each edit becomes an undoable step; changes stay unsaved for the user to review unless `save` is true. Paragraph properties (style, list, alignment) are kept and the new text takes the formatting of the paragraph's first run; character formatting within the paragraph (bold words etc.) is replaced. In text, "\t" is a tab and "\n" a line break within the paragraph. Edit types: "setParagraph" with `paragraph` number and `text`; "insertParagraph" with `after` (paragraph number; the new paragraph copies its properties) and `text`; "deleteParagraph" with `paragraph`; "replaceText" with `find` and `replace` (applied within every editable paragraph containing `find`). Edits are applied in order and paragraph numbers refer to the document as it is when each edit is applied, so an insert or delete shifts the numbers of later paragraphs. If one edit fails, the earlier ones remain applied.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the document, or a path relative to the workspace folder.

paragraph.description: setParagraph/deleteParagraph: paragraph number from the outline.

after.description: insertParagraph: number of the paragraph to insert after.

save.description: Save the file after editing (default false: leave the changes unsaved for review).

languageModelTools.name: officeWorkbench_editPresentation
languageModelTools.userDescription: Edit text in shapes and tables, or duplicate, delete and reorder slides of a PowerPoint presentation.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Edits a PowerPoint presentation (.pptx/.pptm). Read the file first with the read tool and `outline: true`: it lists each slide's editable shapes by id with their paragraphs, and table cells by row and column. The file is opened in the Office Workbench editor and each edit becomes an undoable step; changes stay unsaved for the user to review unless `save` is true. Paragraph properties (bullets, levels, alignment) are kept and new text takes the formatting of the paragraph's first run; paragraphs whose text is unchanged are left as they are. Edit types: "setText" with `slide` (1-based), `shape` (id from the outline) and `paragraphs` (list of strings; "\n" inside one is a line break) or `text` (split into paragraphs at line breaks) — replaces all text of the shape, including empty placeholders; "setTableCell" with `slide`, `shape`, 1-based `row` and `column`, and `paragraphs` or `text`; "replaceText" with `find`, `replace` and optional `slide` (in every editable shape and table cell); "duplicateSlide" / "deleteSlide" with `slide`; "moveSlide" with `slide` and new position `to`. Slide numbers refer to the presentation as it is when each edit is applied. If one edit fails, the earlier ones remain applied.

filePath.description: Absolute path of the presentation, or a path relative to the workspace folder.

shape.description: setText/setTableCell: shape id from the outline.

text.description: setText/setTableCell: the new text, one paragraph per line (alternative to paragraphs).

save.description: Save the file after editing (default false: leave the changes unsaved for review).

officeWorkbench.markdownPdf.browserPath.markdownDescription: Path to the Chromium-based browser (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Chromium, Brave) used by **Export Markdown to PDF**. Leave empty to find one automatically.

officeWorkbench.markdownPdf.pageSize.markdownDescription: Paper size used by **Export Markdown to PDF**.
